goals.primary: Stay healthy to the start line

zones.easy: 130-145 (9:00-10:00); avg to 152 in heat through wk11
zones.threshold: 155-164. Used this cycle in weeks 8 and 12 only, as 3 x 0.5 mi (wk 8) and 3 x 0.75 mi (wk 12) at 7:45 with easy floats. Reps should average 158-165; a rep AVERAGING above 164 means the session went above threshold and should be stopped. 7:45 is the threshold pace here because 8:00-8:15 sits only 15-30 sec/mi off MP 8:30 and is not a distinct stimulus. The 164 anchor comes from the Apr 2025 Jersey City Half (162 avg) and is 15 months old; re-anchor off the Sep 19 check.

tibRules: Flare trigger is SUSTAINED fast pace in the 7:30-7:45 band, not volume or consecutive days. This block deliberately tests the top edge of that band: weeks 8 and 12 prescribe 7:45 in broken reps with easy floats. Everything else stays clear of it. Verified Jul 29 2026 at 8:00-8:15: fastest 400m 7:51, fastest half mile 7:56, fastest mile 8:18, max HR 162 against a threshold of 164. Week 8 (Aug 25) is the decision point for whether 7:45 is viable at all.

Tempo sessions run in weeks 4, 6, 8 and 12 only; no other week carries one. Week 4 (done) and week 6 run at 8:00-8:15 with 8:30 as a bad-day floor. Weeks 8 and 12 run at 7:45 and are conditional: week 12 happens at 7:45 only if week 8's 48-hour check was clean, otherwise it runs at 8:00-8:15. Rep length progresses 3 x 0.5 (wk 4) -> 3 x 0.75 (wk 6) -> 3 x 0.5 at 7:45 (wk 8) -> 3 x 0.75 at 7:45 (wk 12). Rep length drops when pace rises: one variable at a time. Mile reps at 7:45 are deliberately absent from this block. Pace creep is the primary risk; a rep split under 7:38 invalidates the session as a data point. Placement: Wednesday in weeks 4 and 6, Tuesday in weeks 8 and 12 so recovery falls directly after.

Marathon pace 8:30 is the race-specific workhorse and sits 45-60 sec clear of the flare band, which makes added MP volume the cheapest way to add quality. It appears in long-run pace-up segments throughout and in one midweek session, week 13 Wednesday. Dedicated threshold work exists this cycle but only in weeks 8 and 12.
Fast bursts (strides, <=90s reps) are safe but never sprint-fast. Strides run twice weekly throughout.
Long-run pace-up segments are capped at MP (8:30), built gradually within an easy base, and dropped immediately if the knee or tib speaks.

At most one dedicated fast session per week, counting tempo and midweek MP alike, and at most one MP dose within that week's long run. A dose may be delivered as one continuous block or as two blocks separated by an easy float; the broken format is a way of delivering the same dose with less continuous time under tension, not a way of taking two doses. Floats within a long run run at full easy pace, 9:00-10:00; a float run faster than that turns the whole span into a continuous progression run and voids the distinction. Weeks 7 and 9 carry no quality at all; both are travel weeks and that is intentional.
Morning-after check (touch-tenderness + stairs, for both knee and tib) governs progression, not in-run feel.

Instantaneous watch readings are not evidence, for pace or for HR. Watch pace reads fast during efforts and swings hard: the Jul 29 2026 session logged a 5:58 max speed that never happened, and a perceived 7:30 turned out to be 7:56 on the splits. HR behaves the same way; the Jul 25 2026 long run peaked at 168 while averaging 152.7 at a genuinely easy 9:34 pace. Judge both from run averages and lap splits after the fact, never from the number on the wrist mid-run. Momentary HR spikes cresting a hill carry no information.

Heat and humidity drift HR upward at unchanged pace, and that drift is real cardiovascular strain rather than a measurement error, so the correct response is to slow down, not to work harder. Through week 11, long-run HR may average 150-157 on easy portions and up to 160 within MP segments, and easy weekday runs may average to 152. These are averages across the run, not spot ceilings. Abort gate: if a run's full average exceeds 158 at easy pace, conditions are winning; shorten it or slow it rather than pushing through.

The 164 LT anchor comes from the Apr 2025 Jersey City Half (162 avg) and is about fifteen months old. The Jul 25 2026 easy long run peaked at 168, which means either the anchor has moved or the optical sensor spikes; both are plausible. Every HR zone in this plan inherits that uncertainty. Re-anchor off the Sep 19 sustainability check, which is already built to measure it, and do not widen any HR allowance on the strength of the current number before then.

structure.Base: Weeks 1-5 (Jul 6 - Aug 9): 15.5 -> 23.4 mpw. Week 5 is a flat week at 23.0 rather than a down week; the absolute load does not warrant an unload there. Easy aerobic + strides, knee return protocol wks 1-2, tempo enters wk4. LR 7.6 -> 11; first MP touch in the wk4 long run (Aug 1), repeated at the same 2 mi dose in wk5.
structure.Build: Weeks 6-11 (Aug 10 - Sep 20): 27 -> 37 mpw, dipping to 23.5 in the wk9 travel cutback. Volume sits in midweek rather than in longer long runs, which keeps the long run well under half the week. Tempo in wks 6 and 8, with wk8 the first 7:45 exposure. MP (8:30) segments grow inside the long run. LR 12.5 -> 18. Wk 6 carries the block's highest acute:chronic ratio, though the denominator is understated by the suppressed weeks 1-3.
structure.Peak: Weeks 12-14 (Sep 21 - Oct 11): 42 -> 46 mpw with a long-run unload at wk13 (38 mpw, LR 15). LR 20 / 15 / 22, the 22 on Oct 10. Tempo in wk12 only, on Tuesday; wk14 carries none. Wk13 holds the block's only midweek MP session, and its midweek volume keeps the step into wk14 at +21 percent.
structure.Taper: Weeks 15-17 (Oct 12 - Nov 1): volume drops to 30/24, then race week (~38 incl. race), short MP (8:30) touches to stay sharp, race Nov 1

weeks.label: Long run steps to 11 · first MP touch

days.focus: Full rest. Structural, not conditional. Morning tib check: touch-tenderness + first flight of stairs.

1 mi easy, then 3 x 0.5 mi @ 8:00-8:15 with a 0.5 mi easy float between each, then 1 mi easy to finish. 4.5 mi total, inclusive of planned mileage. Broken reps rather than one continuous mile, per PT guidance: shorter bouts limit continuous time under tension while the stimulus is new. The shorter format is not permission to run faster. Each half mile should land in 4:00-4:07; if they drift into the 3:50s you are in the flare band and should back off. Drop to easy if the knee or tib speaks; the morning-after check governs.

7 mi easy, then 2 mi @ 8:30 (MP), then 2 mi easy. Biggest step on the long-run ladder so far (8.5 to 11) and the first MP touch, so keep every easy mile genuinely easy. The course is hilly, so run the MP segment by effort rather than by the number: hold the effort on the climbs and let the pace slide, and do not chase the time back on the descents. Expect HR a few beats above the Jul 25 flat-course baseline of 152.7 avg; that is terrain, not a problem. Cutting the MP block to 1 mile is a planned option, not a failure; take it if the legs or the hills say so. Drop to easy entirely if the knee or tib speaks. Fuel every 30-40 min.

FIRST 7:45 EXPOSURE. About 1.5 mi easy warm-up including the full tib protocol, then 3 x 0.5 mi @ 7:45 with 0.5 mi easy floats between, then easy to finish. 6 mi total, inclusive. Fast volume is 1.5 mi.

This is the first session in the 7:30-7:45 band, so rep length drops back to half miles to buy the pace increase: one variable at a time, and you do not get to progress pace and rep length in the same session.

Rationale: 8:00-8:15 sits only 15-30 sec/mi off MP and is not a distinct physiological stimulus. Half pace from Apr 2025 was 7:28, which puts true LT near 7:45, so this is a genuine threshold session rather than brisk marathon pace.

THREE GATES, all judged on split averages, never on the watch mid-run:
1. HR: expect reps averaging 158-165. If any single rep AVERAGES above 164, that was above threshold, not at it. End the session there.
2. Pace: if any rep split comes back under 7:38, that was a 7:30-band session and does not count as a clean data point regardless of how the tib felt.
3. Morning-after: the informative read for tendon work is 48 hours, not 24. Wednesday is rest specifically to give a clean window; Thursday morning is the verdict.

STOP CONDITION: one bad morning-after and the tempo ceiling drops to 8:00-8:15 for the rest of the block. Not 'back off a bit.' The question is closed until the Sep 19 re-anchor, and week 12's session runs at 8:00-8:15.

Rest, placed directly after the first 7:45 session. This is the single most informative day in the block for whether the raised tempo ceiling is viable, and it is the only clean 48-hour tendon window you get: week 12's Wednesday carries volume and cannot be rest. Do not fill this day. Tib check today and again tomorrow morning.
This week's longest weekday run, off a rest day so the legs are fresh for it. Fully easy, then 4 x 20s relaxed strides at the end. Second of this week's two stride days.

9 mi easy, then 2 mi @ 8:30 (MP), then 1 mi easy float, then 2 mi @ 8:30 (MP), then 1 mi easy. 15 mi total, 4 MP miles. First broken-block long run of the block: two MP blocks separated by an easy float rather than one continuous segment. Same logic as the broken tempo reps, applied to race pace: splitting the block buys a fourth MP mile while cutting continuous time under tension, and each block starts fresh so pace does not decay across it. FLOAT DISCIPLINE IS THE WHOLE SESSION. The float mile runs 9:00-10:00, no faster. A float at 8:45 turns this into a 7-mile progression run, which is a materially harder session than the one written and is not what you are testing. Judge it off the splits afterward, not the watch mid-run. Drop the second MP block, or both, to easy if the knee or tib speaks.
Leg strength. Calf raises, tibialis raises, single-leg stability, posterior chain. Directly supports the anterior tib.

days.focus: Full rest. Structural, not conditional. Morning tib check: touch-tenderness + first flight of stairs.

Tempo sits on Tuesday because at 7:45 it cannot sit three days ahead of a 20-miler with 5 MP miles. About 2 mi easy warm-up including the full tib protocol, then 3 x 0.75 mi @ 7:45 with 0.5 mi easy floats, then easy to finish. 8 mi total, inclusive. Fast volume is 2.25 mi.

CONDITIONAL: run this only if week 8's 7:45 session returned a clean 48-hour check. If it did not, this session is 3 x 0.75 mi @ 8:00-8:15 instead and the 7:45 experiment is over for the block.

Rep length steps from 0.5 to 0.75 at the established pace. Mile reps at 7:45 are deliberately not in this plan: the gain over 0.75 at the same pace is small, and what it adds is continuous time under tension at flare-band force, which is exactly what the broken-rep format exists to limit.

Same three gates as week 8: reps averaging 158-165 with a hard stop if any rep averages above 164; no rep split under 7:38; morning-after governs. Note that Wednesday is an easy run this week rather than rest, so the tendon read is softer here than in week 8. Wednesday morning's check, before running, is the one that counts.
Easy aerobic, the day after the tempo. Genuinely easy, no strides, no pace-ups. Do the morning tib check before you run; that check is the week's tendon verdict and running first contaminates it.

Stays CONTINUOUS deliberately, unlike the week 8 and 12 long runs: on fresh midweek legs the useful stimulus is sustained rhythm at race pace, and the broken format exists to manage fatigue that is not present here. MP at 8:30 sits 45-60 sec clear of the flare band, so the tendon cost is low; this is cumulative race-pace volume, which is the variable most worth adding. Comfortable and controlled, not a workout. RACE DAY. Goal 3:43 at 8:30/mi, HR 148-153. Start controlled - bank nothing, let the first 10K feel almost easy. Settle into 8:30, fuel every 30-40 min. The knee and tib have been managed all block; race pace is safely outside your flare zone, so run your race. Adjust to what the day gives: sub-3:50 B-goal, and you beat 3:59 comfortably. Trust the block.
